questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The aspects crucial for my choosing of my destination was the language spoken at the university, location of the university, academic oppurtunities, housing and ratings of the university.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy. Both the University of Copenhagen and the University that I studied on my exchange were very helpful in terms of providing me with the neccessary information for my stay.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I recieved assistance from the person in charge of exchange students. She was very helpful and would answer very quickly on my e-mails.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Both dorms and student appartments.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: At my dorm there was a catina, which i found very nice. The food was very cheap and decent.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is very good for socializing with other students. Both domestic and international students. The rooms at the dorms are quite small, but I found it fine. There are lots of social events at the dorms, which give you the possibility to meet many other people.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: In the start it was quite difficult to find the postgraduate courses. But the person in charge of the exchange students helped me alot, which made the process easy.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You get access to the host institutions website. When you have access you will be able to registrate the courses that you find interesting. When you have picked your courses, you will then get an e-mail from the institution, which tells you whether you have been registrated or not.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The person in charge of the exchange students was availaibe on e-mail to help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was quite succesful I would say. Although for two courses I hadn't got any information about the commencing dates. Those two courses started before i arrived, which meant that I had to pick two new courses before I arrived. That was not big problem, because I found many of the courses availaibe interestning. And I enjoyed the ones that I picked.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would advice the future exchange students to read the course description closely, and also make sure that they know when the courses commence and when they end.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found the level to be appropiate and it reflected what I had also experinced at the University of Copenhagen.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Actually it was quite similar. They also made use of small classes with not to many students, which to a greater extent gave us the opportunity to participate in the discussion in class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Australian legal process and research, Managing high conflict personalities in legal disputes, Transnational Labour Law and Techonology, design and innovation in legal services.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the ones that I took. The curriculum was exciting and the proffessors were very engaged.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They had a nice gym and many different opportunities to join sports.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Gymnastic, Swimming, Gym, Football, Rugby, Zumba, Discussion groups and more.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The gym and the football team.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The Great ocean road, Phillip Islands and the Melbourne Cricket Ground.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I would say that it was quite easy. The Australian people are really nice and welcoming. They will help you settle in and are always interested in talking with you.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Participate in as many events as possible. This will help you socialize easier.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I don't know really. I had a really nice time and I enjoyed living in Australia. If I should find one thing maybe just settling in and getting used to live in another country.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The people that I met and there way of living life.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be open to meet new people, ask for help when you need it and remember to be prepared before your stay in terms of money, housing and ways of transportation for your university.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Bring all types of clothing. The weather in Melbourne change a lot.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Studying in another country with another legal system, improving my english and meeting new people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not having my friends from home to enjoy this fantastic experince with me.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
